detail.longDescription: I want to create a static body in Pymunk. I've been using pymunk.Body so far: space = pymunk.Space() body = pymunk.Body(body_type=pymunk.Body.STATIC) shape = pymunk.Circle(body, radius=10) space.add(body, shape) But I recently learnt that space has its own static body space.static_body : space = pymunk.Space() shape = pymunk.Circle(space.static_body, radius=10) space.add(shape) From the docs : property static_body: Body A dedicated static body for the space. You don’t have to use it, but many times it can be convenient to have a static body together with the space. Another docs page : Static bodies are bodies that never (or rarely) move. [...] Every space provide [sic] a built-in static body for your convenience. It certainly is very convenient, as I don't need to manually create a static body now. In that case, why do we still have pymunk.Body(body_type=pymunk.Body.STATIC) ? In what situation would I need to create a static body manually?
